name: card-flip-physics
title: Card Flip (physics)
description: A two-sided ticket card that turns over on a drag, a flick or the keyboard, with visible thickness and a moving band of light. The front lists event details; the back carries a QR code.
use: A ticket, pass or membership card should feel physical and reveal a code on its back.
avoid: Front and back are fixed ticket templates; real content needs front and back nodes swapped in.
a11y: Focus ring, keyboard flip and a spoken hint are present; reduced-motion lands it on a face without spinning. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: respected)
looks: A tall, dark ticket card with orange accents sits on black. The front shows Admit one, a GA badge, the event name in bold and small date, venue and holder details; the back shows a white QR code with gate, row and seat fields.
behaves: Dragging the card spins it on its vertical axis and releasing lets a spring settle it flat on the nearer face. A highlight sweeps across the surface as it turns, and the floor shadow narrows edge-on.
customise: Pass front and back nodes plus axis, label and controlled flipped state; the default ticket layout and colour palette live in the source.
weight: light: A single card; a hand-written spring runs only while it turns.
demo: Ticket for Fieldwork Sessions, Vol. 04, holder Jordan Vale, seat 14, ticket no. 004182.
polishWhy: Convincing thickness, light sweep and sprung settle; ticket text is small but tidy.
